The event forms part of a touring exhibition staged in several cities across north-west France. It caters to both private enthusiasts and trade visitors from the hospitality, retail and catering sectors. The organiser, GL Events Exhibitions Opérations, based in Brest, is an experienced exhibition company known for its professional delivery, thematic range and strong regional roots. At the heart of the fair is the breadth and diversity of French wine culture. Producers from renowned regions including Bordeaux, Burgundy, the Loire Valley, Provence, Alsace and Champagne present red, white and rosé wines, alongside sweet specialities and sparkling wines. All products are available for tasting and purchase on site. The format is deliberately practical and dialogue-driven: visitors taste wines in direct conversation with the growers, receive detailed information on grape varieties, vinification methods, vintage characteristics and food pairings, and often benefit from special show offers. As a result, the event serves not only as a retail platform but also as an opportunity to deepen one’s understanding of terroir, craftsmanship and regional identity. The wine offering is complemented by a carefully curated selection of gourmet products. Exhibitors from the delicatessen, cheesemaking, charcuterie, foie gras, chocolate, spice and tea sectors showcase high-quality goods closely linked to their regions of origin. Many are produced artisanally, in some cases using sustainable methods, reflecting growing consumer demand for transparency and quality. Themed visitor trails provide guidance, for example highlighting organic producers or wine tourism operators presenting stays at vineyards and gastronomic travel experiences. The fair is of particular significance to Brittany and to Quimper in particular. It combines French gastronomic heritage with local hospitality and attracts substantial visitor numbers each year from the surrounding area and beyond. Highlights include exclusive tastings, personal recommendations from producers and themed presentations exploring current trends in the wine sector. Exhibitors primarily represent the wine and spirits industries, gourmet food production, farm-direct sales and culinary tourism. The visitor profile ranges from quality-conscious private buyers to trade professionals from the hospitality industry, specialist wine merchants and retail, all seeking new products and suppliers. This blend creates an atmosphere that bridges the gap between a consumer fair and an industry marketplace. As part of a broader touring exhibition programme, Aux Vignobles! enhances the profile of French premium products across multiple cities and supports regional producers. The Parc des Expositions Quimper-Cornouaille offers modern exhibition halls, sound infrastructure and ample parking. It is easily accessible via Brittany’s main roads as well as by public transport from the town centre, providing an appropriate setting for an event that brings together fine food and wine, professional expertise and direct personal exchange.

The "Aux Vignobles!" trade fair, formerly known as "Salon Vins & Gastronomie", is an annual highlight for wine enthusiasts and gourmets, held in several cities across northwestern France. Organized by GL Events Exhibitions Opérations, based in Brest, the event provides both industry professionals and the general public with a unique opportunity to discover the diversity and authenticity of French wines and gastronomic specialties. For the city of Metz, "Aux Vignobles!" is a significant economic driver. The fair attracts not only professionals, traders, and restaurateurs from across France but also numerous connoisseurs and tourists who travel specifically for the event. Although Metz itself is not a wine-producing region, its proximity to renowned vineyards such as Alsace, Champagne, and Moselle makes it a natural meeting point for winemakers, merchants, and wine lovers. Thanks to its strategic location in the Grand Est region and its close ties to Germany, Luxembourg, and Belgium, Metz is exceptionally well-connected. The TGV links the city to Paris in just 90 minutes, and direct road and rail connections make travel easy both nationally and internationally. At the heart of the event is a deep appreciation for the evolving French terroir, whose regional characteristics give it a distinctive appeal. Artisan producers from across France showcase their creations, invite visitors to tastings, and offer direct purchases of their specialties. Guests benefit from the expertise of winemakers and producers, exclusive trade fair deals, and fascinating insights into the production process. A strong emphasis is placed on sustainability and organic cultivation. Many winemakers with organic certification present their wines, while dedicated tasting areas enhance the sensory experience. Wine tourism also plays a central role, with wineries welcoming visitors, offering insights into winemaking, and presenting tourism packages that allow guests to experience the cultural heritage of wine firsthand. In addition to an extensive selection of wines, the fair features a carefully curated array of French delicacies. Specialties such as foie gras, fine charcuterie, artisanal cheeses, chocolates, pastries, and exquisite spices invite visitors to indulge. These culinary delights create harmonious pairings of food and wine, highlighting the excellence of French gastronomy. More than just a traditional consumer fair, "Aux Vignobles!" is a tribute to French culinary culture, offering an invitation to experience the country’s rich gastronomic heritage in a convivial atmosphere. Blending tradition with modernity, craftsmanship with innovation, the event provides both connoisseurs and newcomers with the opportunity to expand their knowledge of wine and cuisine. Set against the unique backdrop of each host city, the fair promises an enjoyable and educational experience for all who share a passion for fine wines and exquisite food.

The Whisky Fair Rhein-Ruhr is a premier event for whisky enthusiasts and industry experts. Since its inception in 2014, it has been one of Düsseldorf’s annual highlights. As a unique blend of trade fair and public exhibition, it brings together a diverse range of exhibitors and visitors. Distilleries, importers, specialist retailers, and independent bottlers showcase the latest trends and exquisite whisky specialties. Organized by Rolf Kaspar GmbH, a distinguished company in the whisky industry known for its expertise, quality, and exclusive selection, the fair offers visitors the opportunity to sample high-quality whiskies from around the world. Guests can participate in professional tastings and attend expert-led seminars where industry professionals share valuable insights. Collectors and connoisseurs also have the chance to discover rare bottlings and limited editions. The event takes place at Classic Remise Düsseldorf, a stunning industrial landmark with a unique atmosphere. Typically serving as an exhibition space for classic cars, this stylish venue provides the perfect setting for an exclusive whisky experience. Düsseldorf stands out as a host city with excellent accessibility and a vibrant cultural scene. In addition to exceptional whisky selections, visitors can enjoy a carefully curated culinary program that complements the tasting experience. The Whisky Fair Rhein-Ruhr is more than just a trade show—it is an immersive event for those who appreciate whisky in all its diversity and wish to deepen their knowledge.

The " Premium Food Show " is an annual trade fair held at Tokyo Big Sight, Japan's largest exhibition and convention center in Tokyo. It is organized by the Premium Food Show Executive Committee in collaboration with the First Co., Ltd. Global Business Promotion Division, attracting experts from the global food industry. The fair focuses on showcasing Halal products, vegan and plant-based foods, gluten-free, and organic foods, thus reflecting the latest trends and developments in these rapidly growing segments. This product range not only addresses the growing global demands for healthy and ethical nutrition but also considers specific dietary needs and preferences. The Premium Food Show is distinguished by a series of seminars and conferences that impart the latest expertise and highlight current topics in the food industry. Numerous industry representatives, including producers, traders, and buyers of specialty foods, as well as restaurateurs and hoteliers, use the fair to explore new business opportunities. The event strongly reflects its connection with the host city Tokyo, known for its culinary diversity and innovation. The venue, Tokyo Big Sight, offers excellent infrastructure and is easily accessible both by public transport and by car. In summary, the Premium Food Show is a central meeting point for professionals looking to exchange information on the latest developments, products, and services in the food industry. It provides a platform to discover innovative solutions that will significantly influence both the market and the lifestyle of consumers.

DRINK SEOUL is South Korea’s premier trade fair for the national and international beverage industry. Held annually at the renowned COEX Convention and Exhibition Center in Seoul – one of Asia’s most advanced venues for exhibitions and events – the show is organized by the Global MICE Experts Group (GMEG), a seasoned provider of international B2B trade events with a strong focus on networking platforms. As a central industry meeting point for manufacturers, distributors, buyers, and professionals from the beverage, food, and hospitality sectors, DRINK SEOUL offers a high-caliber platform to showcase and discover the latest trends, technologies, and products. Exhibitors range from breweries, wineries, and spirits producers to makers of traditional Korean beverages, as well as suppliers of raw materials, machinery, equipment, franchise concepts, and retail technologies. The fair also features MD products, by-products, and specialized services such as training and consulting. A particular emphasis is placed on the diverse and innovative world of beverages – from craft beer and premium spirits to trending non-alcoholic drinks – and on the fusion of traditional brewing and distilling craftsmanship with forward-thinking product design. DRINK SEOUL positions itself not only as a trade fair, but also as a source of inspiration, a trend monitor, and a professional development hub. Masterclasses, seminars, and tasting sessions covering categories such as wine, sake, mead, and soju provide deep insights into the history, production methods, and sensory characteristics of these drinks. International competitions and cultural showcases – including those held in parallel with the Korea International Beer Expo (KIBEX) – make the event an immersive experience, highlighting Korea’s cultural identity as a country rich in tradition yet open to innovation. The combination of business matching, networking events, and knowledge-sharing opportunities makes DRINK SEOUL especially valuable for decision-makers in sales, retail, gastronomy, hospitality, as well as importers, export agencies, and franchise providers. DRINK SEOUL offers a prominent stage for both local start-ups and global brands to position themselves in the dynamic South Korean market and build sustainable partnerships. The venue – COEX in Seoul’s Gangnam district – is easily accessible via several subway lines and ideally situated amidst hotels, restaurants, and shopping areas, making it convenient for both domestic and international visitors. Anyone who doesn’t want to miss the next big development in the beverage industry can’t afford to overlook DRINK SEOUL.

개최장소(베뉴): WTCMM World Trade Center Metro Manila
축제소개: The "Philippine Food Expo" (PFE) is a leading trade fair for the Philippine food and beverage industry. It serves as a central platform for producers, traders, and investors to showcase and discuss innovations, trends, and market opportunities in the agricultural and food sectors. Organized by PHILFOODEX INC., the expo takes place annually at the World Trade Center Metro Manila, bringing together key industry players. A particular focus is placed on evolving consumer habits, influenced by rising incomes, urbanization, and population growth. The expo highlights the challenges and opportunities of globalization in the food trade while emphasizing sustainable solutions. Companies present strategies to enhance productivity, optimize resource utilization, and ensure a stable market demand. The extensive range of products includes a variety of beverages such as juices, coffee, tea, milk, wine, and spirits, as well as baked goods, dairy products, chilled and frozen foods, confectionery, and fresh and processed fruits and vegetables. Additionally, seafood, herbs, organic health foods, and modern food equipment and accessories are featured. The expo portfolio is further enriched by packaging and labeling solutions, franchising, industry publications, packaging design, and distribution management. As a result, the Philippine Food Expo serves as a comprehensive platform for manufacturers, distributors, restaurateurs, and retailers. One of the standout features of the expo is its interactive special events, distinguishing it from other industry fairs. These include culinary competitions for students and faculty in hospitality management and culinary arts, featuring disciplines such as food styling and photography, healthy pasta, and Philippine regional table setting. The program is complemented by professional and business seminars offering valuable insights into current market strategies and industry developments. An investment forum provides new business perspectives, while targeted media exposure ensures broad public awareness. The Philippine Food Expo is not only a showcase for Philippine products but also highlights Manila's role as a hub for the food industry in Southeast Asia. It brings together professionals from production, distribution, gastronomy, retail, and technology, all seeking new business opportunities, partnerships, and innovative solutions. As a national flagship event, it sets industry benchmarks and contributes to the advancement of the country’s agricultural and food sectors. The venue, the World Trade Center Metro Manila, is situated in an economically vibrant region with excellent infrastructure. The expo is easily accessible from the Ninoy Aquino International Airport and Manila’s major business districts. This makes the Philippine Food Expo not only a must-attend event for industry professionals but also a gateway to one of Asia’s fastest-growing food markets.

Spring at Trebsen Castle is not a traditional trade fair, but a high-quality public event with an exhibition character. Held annually in spring, it deliberately focuses on inspiration, atmosphere and quality. The event is organised by ARCOS GmbH, an experienced curator of sophisticated lifestyle and castle events. With a keen eye for distinctive locations, coherent themes and clearly defined audiences, ARCOS creates exceptional visitor experiences. Each spring, the late-Gothic Trebsen Castle in the Leipzig district is transformed into an elegant world of inspiration, where visitors can stroll through thoughtfully designed state rooms and the idyllic inner courtyard, gathering fresh ideas for the season ahead. The exhibition centres on spring-themed interior and garden ideas, contemporary living, artistic decorations, curated gift ideas, as well as fashion, jewellery and accessories. A selection of hand-picked culinary specialities completes the experience, adding a pleasurable gastronomic dimension. The products and services on display are drawn primarily from the fields of home and interior design, gardening and floristry, arts and crafts, design, fashion, artisan food producers and creative lifestyle concepts. While the event has a strong regional connection to Saxony and the Leipzig area, it also attracts exhibitors and visitors from across central Germany. It is aimed in particular at private consumers, connoisseurs, style-conscious families, home and garden enthusiasts, and culturally minded visitors who value quality, individuality and a distinctive setting. Trebsen Castle enjoys a picturesque location on the banks of the River Mulde, just a few kilometres east of Leipzig, and is easily accessible by car and public transport alike. It provides the ideal backdrop for welcoming spring in style and finding fresh inspiration.

Vinobile is an annual wine fair with a clear mission: to offer wine lovers and connoisseurs a high-quality and enjoyable experience – right in the heart of Feldkirch, Austria. Since its inception in 1998, the event has grown into one of the most important wine fairs in the Lake Constance region. The name “Vinobile” combines the Italian words vino (wine) and nobile (noble), perfectly encapsulating the event’s ambition: noble wine in an elegant setting. The fair takes place at the Montforthaus Feldkirch, an architecturally striking venue located in the city’s historic center. Every spring, traditionally in April, it provides the ideal stage for more than 130 winemakers to present their wines – from emerging talents to established wineries representing all Austrian wine-growing regions. The offering is complemented by selected international vineyards from the Lake Constance area showcasing their specialties. Vinobile is organized by Stadtkultur und Kommunikation Feldkirch, an institution dedicated to promoting cultural diversity and regional value creation. As such, the fair is more than just a platform for presenting wines – it is a cultural event with deep regional roots. Increasing focus is also being placed on organic and biodynamic viticulture, a topic that resonates with both industry professionals and curious wine enthusiasts, while reflecting current trends in the wine sector. A highlight of the program is the Vorarlberg Wine Award, which honors outstanding wines from the region. This recognition reinforces the fair’s commitment to quality and places a spotlight on the work of local winemakers. Alongside tastings and direct exchange with producers, the opportunity to purchase wine on-site has also become a popular feature – offering a refined shopping experience in a sophisticated setting. Vinobile is aimed at professionals from the gastronomy and hospitality sectors, as well as private visitors with a passion for fine wine. The Montforthaus is centrally located in Feldkirch’s Old Town, fully accessible, and easily reached by public transport or car. Anyone seeking an authentic, rich, and atmospheric wine experience will find not only exceptional wines at Vinobile, but also an inspiring space for connection, enjoyment, and discovery.

The VDP.Weinbörse is a trade fair for top-quality German wines and a key meeting point for industry professionals from retail, gastronomy, and the media. Organized annually by the Association of German Prädikat Wine Estates (Verband Deutscher Prädikats- und Qualitätsweingüter, VDP), the event takes place at the Rheingoldhalle in Mainz. Admission is reserved exclusively for trade visitors. As a platform for quality, innovation, and exchange, the VDP.Weinbörse brings together nearly all of the 202 VDP estates from across Germany under one roof. Winemakers present their latest vintages in person, offering a compelling insight into German wine culture at its finest. Alongside established grape varieties such as Riesling and Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir), the focus also includes developments such as biodynamic viticulture, orange wines, indigenous grape varieties, and sustainable winegrowing concepts that combine ecological responsibility with economic viability. Visitors can expect not only an exclusive selection of wines but also in-depth expertise delivered through hands-on masterclasses. Whether it’s emerging trends in German Pinot Noir, the renaissance of Riesling, or the future of sustainable viticulture, the VDP.Weinbörse provides valuable, practice-oriented knowledge at a high professional level. This depth of content makes the event an indispensable resource for meaningful industry exchange. Professionals from across Europe—including winemakers, merchants, restaurateurs, sommeliers, and journalists—use the fair as an opportunity for direct dialogue, networking, and developing new business relationships. The VDP.Weinbörse is considered a reliable indicator of vintage quality and a trendsetter for the German wine industry. It also plays an important role for the city of Mainz, which, as the wine capital of Rheinhessen, offers excellent transport connections by train, car, or plane due to its central location. The Rheingoldhalle, situated directly on the Rhine and just steps from the historic old town, provides an ideal setting for the event. For anyone seeking a comprehensive overview of Germany’s wine elite—combined with top-tier tasting, information, and networking—the VDP.Weinbörse is an unmissable occasion.

Vyno Dienos (Wine Days) is the largest and most prestigious wine fair in the Baltic region. Held annually at LITEXPO, the Lithuanian Exhibition and Congress Centre in Vilnius—the capital of Lithuania—the event has, since its inception in 2005, become a major meeting point for industry professionals and wine enthusiasts aged 20 and above. It has gained international recognition and is organized by Vyno Klubas, a dedicated Lithuanian organization committed to promoting wine knowledge and culture, widely regarded as a leading force in the industry. More than just a showcase for global wine trends, Vyno Dienos plays a key role in supporting Lithuania’s young but rapidly growing wine scene. It brings together wine lovers, winemakers, importers, distributors, and experts from both Lithuania and abroad, offering a unique platform for professional exchange, product discovery, and sensory experiences. The event primarily focuses on European wines, complemented by a curated selection of sparkling wines, mead, and craft beers. A standout feature of the fair is its guided tastings, where attendees can interact directly with producers and sample rare or newly released wines. The tasting experience is enriched by a thoughtfully selected range of gourmet foods and delicacies that pair perfectly with the wines on offer. The event also features a diverse educational program, including workshops, seminars, and expert-led lectures—some geared toward sommelier training—designed to deepen wine knowledge at an advanced level. In addition, the fair showcases wine accessories and cutting-edge technologies related to wine production and storage. Visitors also gain insights into wine tourism opportunities and destinations, appealing to both private travelers and tour operators. Networking events further encourage direct connections between producers, trade professionals, and retailers, creating fertile ground for new collaborations. With its blend of international scope, regional focus, high-quality educational content, and immersive tasting experiences, Vyno Dienos stands out as a one-of-a-kind wine fair—a must-attend annual event for industry experts and passionate wine lovers alike. Admission to the fair is strictly permitted only to persons aged 20 and over.

Bellavita Milano is an international trade fair dedicated to showcasing and promoting Italian food and beverages. It takes place annually at Fiera Milano (Rho) in Rho, a prominent and accessible venue that serves as a hub for international trade and cultural events. The trade fair is organized by Bellavita Expo Ltd. and is part of an extensive series of Bellavita events that take place in other cities worldwide, highlighting the global reach and international character of the fair. The fair offers a variety of main themes and covers a wide range of product categories, including wines and spirits, cheeses and dairy products, meats and sausages, fish and seafood, fruits and vegetables, confections, as well as gourmet and convenience foods. Additionally, specialized segments such as organic, vegan, and "free-from" products, along with dressings, sauces, and spreads, are showcased. The fair holds significant cultural and economic importance for the Milan region, known for its cultural diversity and interest in international culinary trends. This makes it an ideal location for such an event. One of the highlights of Bellavita Milano is the numerous competitions, tastings, and award ceremonies where companies can present their products and win accolades. These events attract more exhibitors and visitors each year and enhance the prestige of the fair. Exhibitors come from various sectors of the Italian food industry, while the main visitors are professionals from gastronomy, retail, and wholesale, who are always on the lookout for new products and trends. In summary, Bellavita Milano is more than just a fair. It serves as a central platform for the Italian food and beverage industry and offers a unique opportunity to experience the diversity and quality of Italian products in a dynamic and international setting.

Langres Gastronomique is an annual highlight for food lovers, producers, and enthusiasts of regional culinary culture. Held at the Salle Jean-Favre in Langres—a historic town in northeastern France—the event is organized by the dedicated Association Langres Foires et Salons , which is committed to promoting the region’s economy, culture, and way of life. This fair is much more than a marketplace – it serves as a vibrant showcase of the terroir , the culinary and artisanal identity of the Langres region. Numerous passionate exhibitors present their specialties, ranging from artisan cheeses and air-dried sausages to homemade pasta, honey, syrups, and premium ice cream. Visitors are not only invited to sample the products but also to engage directly with the producers – an experience that defines the unique character of the event. What further sets Langres Gastronomique apart is its successful blend of gastronomy, culture, and entertainment. The program includes cooking demonstrations, culinary competitions, and live tastings, along with musical performances, evening events, and interactive experiences for both children and adults. Workshops, talks, and hands-on activities add extra depth, turning a visit into a well-rounded and memorable experience. The fair is deliberately focused on quality over quantity, emphasizing regional food craftsmanship and artisanal products. Most exhibitors come from the fine food, specialty food production, and artisan sectors. The primary audience includes culinary professionals, hoteliers, retailers, and food enthusiasts seeking authentic products, new business contacts, or fresh culinary inspiration. Langres Gastronomique reflects the history, craftsmanship, and zest for life of the region. It plays a key role in promoting local products and producers while strengthening regional identity and pride. The centrally located Salle Jean-Favre is easily accessible by car and public transport. For anyone wishing to experience the authentic spirit of French culinary culture combined with regional diversity and a rich cultural program, Langres Gastronomique is a must-attend event on the culinary calendar.

The Gourmet Selection is an annual trade fair that has established itself as a key event in the international fine food industry since its inception in 2009. It is organized by Comexposium, one of the world’s leading trade show organizers. This exclusive event has become a highly specialized platform for delicacies, gourmet products, and culinary innovations. Held at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles—one of Europe’s largest and most modern exhibition centers—it benefits from a central location in the French capital, a city synonymous with gastronomy, lifestyle, and refined enjoyment. Excellent access to public transport ensures convenient travel for trade visitors from both France and abroad. At the heart of the fair are quality, craftsmanship, and origin. A carefully curated selection of specialties from France and around the world is showcased—ranging from characterful cheeses, premium charcuterie, foie gras, preserves, artisanal chocolates and pralines, fine pastries, and specialty breads to exquisite wines, craft spirits, and innovative non-alcoholic beverages. The event celebrates not only culinary excellence and artisanal quality but also reflects current trends such as plant-based nutrition, “free-from” products, sustainable snacking, and features on guest regions from across the globe. A distinctive feature of the fair is the strong presence of products with protected designations of origin, such as AOP, AOC, or IGP, alongside a wide range of certified organic goods carrying the AB label. Sustainability and transparent sourcing are integral to the concept of the fair and are reflected throughout the product offerings and presentations. In addition to food, the event also includes offerings related to gastronomy and fine food retail, including stylish tableware, premium packaging solutions, and digital tools for the point of sale. The fair is exclusively open to professional visitors—particularly those from the fine food trade, premium grocery retail, concept stores, as well as upscale restaurants and the hospitality sector. A highlight of the event is the “Gourmet Selection Best Of” competition, which honors outstanding and particularly innovative products—a recognized mark of quality and creativity. The fair experience is further enhanced by the Tasting Forum, where fine foods are prepared and sampled live, and the Experts’ Agora, a space dedicated to professional exchange and knowledge transfer. With its clear focus, exceptional product selection, international reach, and the unique atmosphere in the heart of Paris, Gourmet Selection offers a specialized platform for those seeking to combine excellence, innovation, and high-end indulgence.

The Bellavita Expo in Vienna is an annual international trade fair dedicated to the presentation and promotion of Italian food and beverages. The fair is organized by Bellavita Expo Ltd. It is part of a broader series of Bellavita events held worldwide in cities. This underscores the global significance and international character of the fair. The Bellavita Expo Miami aims to connect Italian food producers and exporters with an international professional audience from the gastronomy, retail, and wholesale sectors. The main themes of the fair are diverse and include a wide range of product categories, such as wines and spirits, cheeses and dairy products, meats and sausages, fish and seafood, fruits and vegetables, confectioneries, as well as gourmet and convenience products. Additionally, specialized segments like organic, vegan, and "free-from" products, as well as dressings, sauces, and spreads, are presented. One of the highlights of the Bellavita Expo are the numerous competitions, tastings, and award ceremonies, where companies can showcase their products and win awards. These events attract more exhibitors and visitors each year and enhance the prestige of the fair. The exhibitors come from various sectors of the Italian food industry, while the main visitors are professionals from gastronomy, retail, and wholesale sectors who are always looking for new products and trends. In summary, the Bellavita Expo in Vienna i is more than just a fair. It serves as a central platform for the Italian food and beverage industry and offers a unique opportunity to experience the diversity and quality of Italian products in a dynamic and international setting.

Nouvelle Moselle is a specialised natural wine fair with a clear regional focus. At the same time, it positions itself as a cultural wine festival that reimagines the Mosel not only as a place of origin, but as a shared philosophy and a forward-looking space for artisanal winemaking. Rather than presenting itself as a large, cross-industry trade show, Nouvelle Moselle is deliberately conceived as a curated platform for serious natural wine. The event takes place at the Mosel Vinothek & Winebar in Traben-Trarbach — a venue that, like few others, embodies the historical and economic significance of Mosel wine. The fair is organised by DIE MOSEL Restaurant & Weinbar, a hospitality concept that brings together top regional wines, culinary excellence and cultural programming. Nouvelle Moselle creates an environment in which producers, trade professionals and engaged wine lovers meet and exchange ideas on equal terms. At its core, the fair treats natural wine as an expression of a conscious philosophy. The focus is on organically or biodynamically farmed wines, fermented with indigenous yeasts and bottled with minimal sulphur additions. Synthetic fertilisers, herbicides and technical interventions that might obscure the character of the terroir are consistently avoided. The event combines tasting and knowledge-sharing: visitors sample current releases, single-vineyard and estate wines, pét-nats, skin-contact whites and unfiltered Rieslings, while engaging directly with the growers. Practical discussions explore topics such as vineyard management, soil health, agroforestry systems and the history of the Mosel wine trade. In dedicated “Deep Talks”, the question “What is natural wine?” is examined in depth, providing clarity around a term that is often used loosely. Beyond wine, the fair also showcases products and services from related sectors, including sustainable vineyard technology, specialist publications, hospitality concepts, regional artisan foods and consultancy on biodynamic viticulture and marketing. Exhibitors are drawn primarily from wine production, hospitality, wine retail and sustainable agriculture. The core audience comprises sommeliers, specialist merchants, restaurateurs, journalists, wine consultants and discerning private buyers seeking authentically crafted wines with a clear sense of origin. Choosing Traben-Trarbach as the host location is about more than geography. Once a major centre of the international wine trade, the town uniquely combines Art Nouveau architecture, dramatic river scenery and a deep-rooted wine culture. The Mosel Vinothek & Winebar is centrally located and easily accessible by car via the B53, by rail and through nearby airports. As such, Nouvelle Moselle offers more than a professional tasting event: it delivers an immersive experience in one of Germany’s most historic wine regions — a place where natural wine is not a passing trend, but part of a sustainable and forward-looking future.

The Summer Fancy Food Show is North America’s largest trade fair for specialty foods and is regarded as a showcase for innovation, quality, and artisanal craftsmanship in the world of culinary products. Since its inception in 1955, it has evolved into a key meeting point for the international food industry. The term “Fancy Food” not only signifies unique and premium products but also stands for high standards in taste, originality, and product quality – from exquisite delicacies to cutting-edge nutrition concepts. Every summer, the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in the heart of Manhattan opens its doors to trade visitors from around the globe. This modern, well-equipped venue impresses with its central location, close to iconic landmarks such as Times Square and Central Park. Excellent access to public transportation makes the Javits Center easily reachable – a clear advantage for international attendees. The event is organized by the Specialty Food Association (SFA) , a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting independent food producers and recognizing outstanding products. But the Summer Fancy Food Show is much more than just a product exhibition: it serves as a trendsetter, idea generator, and dynamic business platform. The event concept successfully combines culinary experience, business relevance, and thematic diversity. Across more than 40 product categories – ranging from plant-based foods and gourmet snacks to innovative beverages – visitors gain practical insights into the latest industry developments through tastings, live cooking demonstrations, and curated theme pavilions. Among the highlights are startups and product debuts, as well as dedicated sections such as the Bakery, Confectionery, Snacks & Sweets Pavilion , the Beverage Pavilion , and the Plant-Based Pavilion . Special attention is given to the Spotlight Showcases , which focus on themes like diversity and emerging food trends, and the RangeMe Collection , offering exclusive previews of up-and-coming brands. A standout feature of the show is the lineup of live competitions and award ceremonies. The SFA People Awards honor exceptional individuals in the industry, while the North America Pastry Competition Championship brings together eight chef teams for a sustainability-focused pastry showdown – a must-see event for anyone passionate about the future of dessert cuisine. The show connects manufacturers, distributors, importers, retailers, restaurateurs, and investors with the aim of unlocking new business opportunities, strengthening existing partnerships, and fostering targeted innovation. In just three days, attendees can establish valuable contacts, build collaborations, and close tangible business deals – efficiently, purposefully, and with an eye toward the future. For anyone looking to experience the latest in the food industry, spot trends early, and soak up the energy of New York’s culinary scene, the Summer Fancy Food Show is the place to be – unique, relevant, and truly inspiring.

The Gourmet Festival Cologne is an annual food and drink festival organised by Wellfairs GmbH. Part of a wider event series that also takes place in Düsseldorf and Mönchengladbach, it provides a showcase for exceptional cuisine and distinctive gourmet products. The festival is held in the heart of Cologne, in front of the Chocolate Museum and along the Rheinauhafen waterfront. Its picturesque setting features rows of white pagoda marquees and stylish food trucks arranged along the aptly named “Food Truck Avenue”. Held during the summer months, the Gourmet Festival Cologne is a premium gastronomic event dedicated entirely to food and drink. With a strong emphasis on international, national and regional specialities, it invites visitors to explore a wide range of flavours and purchase high-quality products. The festival brings together exhibitors from across the food and hospitality sector, including renowned restaurateurs, winemakers and artisanal delicatessen producers. Their offerings range from premium food products, fine wines and high-end spirits to freshly prepared dishes and sweet treats. Kitchen equipment and culinary accessories are also on display. Festival highlights include workshops and tasting sessions hosted by exhibitors, as well as live musical performances. The aim is to provide visitors with an unforgettable culinary weekend. The event attracts both food enthusiasts and professionals from the hospitality and food industries. The venue, located at the Chocolate Museum on the banks of the Rhine, is easily accessible by public transport and within walking distance of Cologne city centre. Parking is available in the surrounding area, although visitors are encouraged to use public transport where possible. In summary, the Gourmet Festival Cologne is a captivating event that brings together outstanding culinary experiences and products from the region and beyond. It offers visitors a unique opportunity to discover new flavours, gain inspiration and immerse themselves in the world of fine food and drink. More than simply a celebration of taste, it is a feast for all the senses.

The Foire aux Vins d’Alsace – the Alsace Wine Fair – is much more than a traditional trade or consumer exhibition. It uniquely blends wine culture, business, music, and regional identity, transforming the city of Colmar each summer since 1948 into a vibrant center of cultural and economic life in Alsace. The abbreviation FAV, short for Foire aux Vins d’Alsace , reflects the event’s core theme: Alsatian wine in all its diversity, quality, and tradition. The event takes place at the modern Parc des Expositions de Colmar, which becomes a ten-day magnet for wine enthusiasts, professionals, music lovers, and families every July or August. Organized by Colmar Expo SA in close cooperation with the Chamber of Commerce and the City of Colmar, this prominent event was originally created to revitalize the regional wine industry in the aftermath of World War II. Today, it ranks among the most significant summer festivals in France, drawing attention well beyond the borders of Alsace. At the heart of the fair are the Wines of Alsace, showcased in a dedicated wine trade exhibition featuring more than 1,500 samples, expert tastings, specialist lectures, and the ceremonial election of the Reine des Vins d’Alsace. This sensory experience is complemented by a diverse range of exhibitors—around 350 businesses from sectors such as crafts, fashion, horticulture, gastronomy, mobility, construction, and lifestyle. What sets the Foire aux Vins d’Alsace apart is its unique combination of trade fair, wine festival, and concert venue. International artists take to the open-air stage, creating a festival atmosphere with performances ranging from pop and rock to electronic and hard rock. Additional entertainment—ranging from burlesque and dance performances to children’s programs, cooking shows, and athletic displays—ensures a varied experience for a wide audience. The fair attracts not only trade visitors and business travelers, but also tourists, wine and music lovers, and culture enthusiasts from across France, the German-speaking regions, and beyond. Deeply rooted in the region, the FAV presents itself as a vibrant showcase of Alsatian lifestyle—a platform that unites economic vitality with cultural tradition and expresses regional pride through a celebration of enjoyment. The Parc des Expositions is conveniently located and easily accessible by car, train, or via nearby airports. Colmar itself, a charming and historic town nestled among the vineyards of Alsace, offers with its architecture and hospitality the perfect setting for a fair that brings the spirit of the region to life year after year.

The Gourmet Festival , founded in 2011, is much more than a traditional food fair. It represents a unique, plant-based gourmet and lifestyle experience in the heart of the city. The festival’s name stands for culinary sophistication, sustainable living, and contemporary enjoyment, bringing together exclusive cuisine and inspiring culinary artistry in a special way. Once a year, the renowned Königsallee—Düsseldorf’s lively promenade—becomes a magnet for gourmets, food enthusiasts, industry experts, and all those who appreciate an innovative, vegan-oriented lifestyle. The festival is organized by Wellfairs GmbH, a renowned company known for its professional event management and keen sense of current food trends. The event serves as a platform for exceptional products and services: visitors discover plant-based alternatives to meat, fish, dairy, and cheese, as well as creative snacks, exclusive delicacies, vegan cosmetics, sustainable fashion, and modern kitchen and household appliances. The offerings are further enriched by contributions from the fields of sports, health, leisure, nutrition counseling, media, and literature, all of which together promote a forward-thinking lifestyle. The festival maintains a strong connection to Düsseldorf and the surrounding region. Many exhibitors come from the local area, highlighting the event’s deep roots within the city. Regional specialties, innovative street food concepts, and the inclusion of emerging businesses create a modern, creative atmosphere at the festival. The event appeals to both private gourmets and professional visitors, including decision-makers and trendsetters from gastronomy, hospitality, and retail. As part of a regional event series that also takes place in cities such as Mönchengladbach and Cologne, the Düsseldorf festival sets its own distinctive accents. What makes this event in the center of one of Germany’s most dynamic cities truly special is the combination of top-class cuisine, modern lifestyle, and an urban atmosphere. Its central location on the Königsallee ensures easy accessibility, whether by public transport or by car. The Gourmet Festival Düsseldorf, held annually as a leading trade fair, embodies enjoyment, sustainability, and innovation. Deeply rooted in the city’s way of life, it inspires both visitors and exhibitors with new ideas and current culinary trends.

The Düsseldorf Autumn Festival at Schloss Eller is considered one of the most exclusive lifestyle and cultural fairs in western Germany, attracting numerous visitors each year who appreciate the extraordinary. More than just an event, it serves as a meeting point for those who are passionate about refined living, seeking inspiration, and discovering the latest trends in a stylish setting. The impressive Schloss Eller in Düsseldorf, with its historic architecture and expansive park, provides a remarkable backdrop for this unique fair experience. The festival takes place annually during the transition from late summer to autumn, usually in early September. It is organized by the renowned Reno Müller Veranstaltungen GmbH & Co. KG, a company known for its exclusive events and meticulous attention to detail. In addition to the Autumn Festival, the company hosts other established events such as “Gartenwelt”, “Landpartie”, “Herbstpartie” and “Schloßzauber” at selected locations, offering a diverse portfolio of experience fairs for a discerning audience. At the heart of the Düsseldorf Autumn Festival are the themes of fine food and culinary delights, fashion and jewelry, home and garden, as well as art and lifestyle. Visitors can look forward to an exclusive selection of gourmet foods, fine wines, delicacies, and popular street food specialties. The offerings are complemented by exceptional design objects, accessories, and handcrafted jewelry. For home and garden enthusiasts, exhibitors showcase elegant plants, creative decoration ideas, high-quality furniture, and exclusive garden accessories. Art lovers will find works ranging from arts and crafts to painting and sculpture, providing inspiration for a distinctive lifestyle. With more than 100 carefully selected exhibitors, the Autumn Festival presents a wide range of products and services that invite visitors to discover, experience, and participate. The fair functions not only as a sales platform but also as a trend barometer: those interested in the latest developments can find expert contacts from various sectors—from goldsmiths and wine merchants to gardeners, artists, and designers. Special highlights of the festival include the impressive Prinzensaal and the Salon of Princess Luise, whose historic interiors offer visitors a glimpse into times past. The Autumn Festival at Schloss Eller is deeply rooted in Düsseldorf’s history and underscores the special significance of art and culture in the state capital—a reflection of the region’s creative identity. The festival primarily appeals to culturally interested connoisseurs, lovers of the good life, and professional visitors from the fields of art, fashion, gardening, and gastronomy. They value the opportunity to exchange ideas with like-minded people and to find new inspiration for their own homes and personal lifestyles. Those who attend the Autumn Festival immerse themselves in a world where enjoyment, style, and inspiration are celebrated at the highest level. Schloss Eller itself is not only a historic landmark, but also conveniently accessible—whether by car, public transport, or bicycle. A visit to the Düsseldorf Autumn Festival at Schloss Eller promises a unique fair experience in one of the city’s most impressive locations and leaves lasting memories thanks to its special atmosphere.

축제소개: "Fine Food Australia" represents more than just a name—it's a commitment to quality and excellence. Embracing the "Fine Food" label, the emphasis is on select foods, drinks, and services within the hospitality sector. Established in 1984, this event has become a pivotal gathering for the Australian food and hospitality sectors. It's expertly organised by Diversified Communications Australia, specialists in hosting international fairs and events. Annually in September, "Fine Food Australia" alternates between two renowned venues: the International Convention Centre (ICC) in Sydney and the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre. It showcases the latest trends, products, and innovations that drive the industry. Key features include food specialties, catering, front-of-house equipment, beverages, coffee and tea, bakery tools, hotel and retail tech, dairy insights, and pioneering packaging solutions. A significant portion of exhibitors hail from retail, food service, and hospitality backgrounds. This event allows them to showcase their newest products and services to a vast industry audience. Primarily, it attracts buyers and key decision-makers from the aforementioned sectors, presenting them with an unparalleled opportunity to keep abreast of industry innovations and establish business connections. Concluding, it's worth noting the strategic locations of both venues: the ICC in Sydney and the Convention Centre in Melbourne. Their central positioning coupled with excellent transport links ensures ease of access. The annual city switch offers attendees a unique opportunity to witness the vibrant facets of the Australian food and hospitality industry. Explore "Fine Food Australia" and delve into a realm of culinary innovation and discovery!

The Gourmet Show is Mexico’s leading trade fair for premium food, fine beverages, and culinary lifestyle. Held annually in the heart of Mexico City – at the modern World Trade Center (WTC) – the event attracts culinary professionals, gourmet enthusiasts, and key decision-makers from across the food industry. Organized by Tradex Exposiciones, a seasoned exhibition company with decades of experience, the show has established itself as a benchmark in the sector. Each September, the Gourmet Show provides an exclusive platform for networking, presentation, and culinary exploration. Its clearly defined thematic structure, divided into dedicated exhibition zones known as Pabellones , offers visitors a well-organized experience while spotlighting industry trends and innovations. The Wine Room showcases international wines and premium spirits, while the Agave Fest is dedicated to traditional Mexican agave-based distillates such as tequila and mezcal. With Veganautas , the show also highlights the growing plant-based and vegan movement, reinforcing its commitment to culinary diversity and forward-thinking concepts. The product range is extensive – from artisanal breads, fine cheeses, and charcuterie to fresh seafood, gourmet chocolates, preserves, organic products, and creative culinary ingredients. The offering is further enriched by high-quality oils, vinegars, and international delicacies. Exhibitors include both small-scale producers and established brands from the fine food, gastronomy, hospitality, retail, wholesale, and catering sectors. Beyond business, the Gourmet Show embraces a cultural mission: to promote Mexico’s culinary heritage while bridging tradition and innovation. Through a diverse program of workshops, tastings, and networking events, it creates a vibrant meeting point for chefs, sommeliers, food professionals, and culinary enthusiasts. As Mexico’s premier culinary showcase, the event highlights the country’s rich diversity of products and producers – and in doing so, enhances its international reputation as a destination for gourmet excellence. The centrally located Pepsi Center also provides ideal infrastructure. Its proximity to the WTC, excellent public transport connections, and nearby hotel options make the Gourmet Show not only a culinary highlight but also a logistical success.

Landpartie Schloss Jägersburg is not a conventional trade fair in the strict sense, but a curated public event with an exhibition character that captures the spirit of autumn in all its richness. Rather than focusing on the functional mechanics of a typical fair, it offers an atmospheric marketplace that brings together inspiration, quality and experience. Once a year, the historic grounds of Schloss Jägersburg in Eggolsheim are transformed into a showcase for garden culture, home design, craftsmanship and fine food. The event is organised by ARCOS GmbH, an experienced promoter of high-end lifestyle and country-style events. Great emphasis is placed on the careful selection of exhibitors, a coherent overall concept and a refined setting. As a result, the event clearly distinguishes itself from standard consumer fairs: the priority is quality and curated variety, not a broad-based mass offering. The thematic focus is on autumnal ideas for gardens and living. Visitors can explore seasonal planting schemes, inspiration for garden and landscape design, and selected products relating to plants, outdoor spaces and nature-inspired living. The range is complemented by high-quality home accessories, stylish decorations for house and garden, and handcrafted one-off pieces. Artisans, designers and fashion labels present distinctive products – from textiles and jewellery to statement accessories – that stand apart from industrial mass production. Culinary specialities complete the experience, with savoury dishes, sweet treats and regional delicacies reflecting the flavours of the season. Exhibitors predominantly represent horticulture, floristry, home and lifestyle, arts and crafts, fashion, fine foods and regional artisan producers. The visitor profile is correspondingly diverse: garden enthusiasts, design-conscious consumers, lovers of regional cuisine, local families and culturally and architecturally minded guests who appreciate the unique setting. The event is not aimed at trade professionals; rather, it is designed for discerning private visitors with an appreciation of aesthetics, craftsmanship and gastronomy. A defining feature is the atmosphere of the historic castle estate itself. With its expansive grounds, mature trees and autumnal backdrop, it provides a fitting and evocative setting for the exhibition. The Landpartie is conceived as a space to explore, linger and enjoy over three days – a deliberately unhurried format that combines inspiration with an enjoyable retail experience. At the same time, the event is firmly rooted in the region. It enriches cultural life in Eggolsheim and the wider Franconian area, supports local producers and attracts visitors from across Bavaria and beyond. Landpartie Schloss Jägersburg forms part of a series of comparable events held at selected historic venues, each individually tailored to its location. The venue is easily accessible. Eggolsheim lies in Upper Franconia between Bamberg and Forchheim and can be reached conveniently by car via the A73 motorway as well as by public transport. In this way, Landpartie Schloss Jägersburg brings together regional identity, the pleasures of the autumn season and a quality-driven exhibitor profile in a refined seasonal highlight.

The 'Rohvolution' fair in Speyer stands as a beacon for the raw food nutritional revolution. The name melds the word "Roh", denoting the core essence of the showcased diet, with "Revolution", indicating a transformative shift in nutritional perspectives. Hosted in the scenic city of Speyer, specifically within the town hall, Rohvolution began its journey in 2017. It has since become an annual magnet for raw food aficionados. The fair is orchestrated by RohKöstlich GmbH, esteemed for their event management prowess and deep understanding of raw food nutrition. Central to the fair is the exploration of raw food nutrition. Attendees can delve into a myriad of related products and services. Offerings span from raw food preparation tools like juicers to taste-test opportunities provided by organic producers and fruit vendors. Here, one can relish smoothies, fresh juices, and other raw food delights. What particularly stands out at the Rohvolution are the enlightening lectures and workshops, shedding light on the art of raw food preparation. Exhibitors, ranging from organic farmers to kitchen equipment manufacturers, spotlight their offerings. Among the visitors, one finds nutrition enthusiasts, health-aware individuals, and professionals spanning the spheres of nutrition, gastronomy, and farming. In summary, Speyer's town hall is more than just a venue; it's a nexus point, both accessible by public transport and car. Set against the historic allure of Speyer, the fair is more than an event – it's an odyssey into the realm of mindful and healthful eating." Note: The 'Rohvolution' fair in Speyer is a central event in the raw food revolution, offering attendees a chance to immerse themselves in raw food nutrition, sample delightful products, and learn from experts. Held at a strategic location, it promises not just knowledge but also a unique cultural experience.

Bellavita in Riga is the leading trade fair for Italian food and beverages in the Baltic region. As an exclusive centre of expertise, it showcases authentic culinary experiences from every region of Italy. Each year, it opens its doors at the International Exhibition Centre Kipsala in Riga to industry professionals from gastronomy, retail, and wholesale, who can explore the diversity and quality of Italian products here. Organised by Bellavita Expo Ltd., the fair—whose name stands for "the beautiful life" and the Italian way of living—combines outstanding culinary excellence with a high-quality, internationally oriented business network. The range of products on offer extends from classic specialities such as olive oil, wine, and cheese to innovative delicacies and convenience solutions, always with a focus on premium quality. A key feature is the international buyer and matchmaking programme, organised in cooperation with the Italian Trade Agency (ICE) and the partner fairs Cibus Parma and TuttoFood Milano. This structured format actively promotes connections between exhibitors and buyers from Central and Northern Europe, opening up new business opportunities in the Baltic market. Bellavita Expo also sees itself as a platform for knowledge transfer and industry trends. Blind tastings, competitions, and awards give producers the opportunity to have their products evaluated by experts. Exhibitors from the fields of wine, dairy products, meat and charcuterie, fish, fruit and vegetables, confectionery, and delicatessen meet a qualified audience from trade, gastronomy, and the international import and export sector. The trade fair is part of a successful, internationally expanding series of events that takes place not only in Riga but also at other locations worldwide. The modern Kipsala Exhibition Centre provides ideal conditions—from its central location to the inspiring atmosphere in Latvia's vibrant capital. Bellavita Expo Riga thus serves as the key platform for anyone wishing to experience Italian food trends, build business relationships, and discover premium products for the Baltic market. The Bellavita take place annually, and therefore presumably in September 2027 in Riga.

WineTech , the Australian Wine Industry Trade Exhibition, is the leading trade fair for Australia’s wine sector. Held every three years at the Adelaide Convention Centre, the event takes place in a state-of-the-art venue located in the heart of South Australia’s capital. Its central location offers convenient access to the airport, central train station, hotels, and restaurants. Over time, WineTech has established itself as a key platform for innovation, technology, and professional exchange within the industry. The name “WineTech” symbolically represents the intersection of wine production and technological advancement—an essential driver of the industry’s long-term viability. The exhibition is organised by Expertise Events Pty Ltd., a renowned Australian event organiser known for delivering high-impact, professional trade shows. Its triennial schedule ensures a steady stream of fresh ideas, technological breakthroughs, and practical solutions to both current and emerging challenges. At the core of WineTech are practical innovations in viticulture and oenology, spanning the entire production process—from vineyard management and modern winemaking technologies to sustainable packaging and bottling solutions. Exhibitors from fields such as automation, sensor technology, robotics, IoT, laboratory analytics, and microbiome science showcase their latest developments, alongside contributions from research institutions, life sciences, and agricultural technology. High-interest topics include precision viticulture, CO₂-reduced materials, data-driven processes, and climate-resilient cultivation methods. The exhibition is further enriched by high-level workshops, interactive floor talks, and the accompanying Australian Wine Industry Technical Conference. These formats create a unique knowledge platform that brings together hands-on professionals, scientists, and industry leaders. Visitors from across the entire value chain—from production to export—attend the event to gain insights, exchange ideas, and make informed investment decisions. WineTech is not a travelling exhibition but a firmly established event rooted in Adelaide. As the capital of South Australia—home to the country’s most productive wine-growing regions—Adelaide offers an ideal setting. Its proximity to renowned wineries, research centres, and innovative start-ups provides the perfect backdrop for a trade fair that embraces both tradition and transformation. Whether the goal is to future-proof operations, develop sustainable vineyards, or gain a competitive edge in global markets, WineTech offers a practical, inspiring, and unparalleled platform for actively shaping the future of the wine industry.
